records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Started near Kilpisjärvi Visitor Centre and reported the first day to Saarijärvi as just over 12 km. Tented in the Saarijärvi hut yard. Confirms the old Saarijärvi hut was closed and the 2023 open/reservable huts were in use.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Return day Saarijärvi-Kilpisjärvi listed as 12 km. Route was rocky/wet but relatively straightforward, briefly entered Norway, reached Tsahkaljärvi before a final gravel-road descent to Kilpisjärvi Visitor Centre. Endpoint evidence: old Saarijärvi hut was closed and the new hut was a couple hundred meters back.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Used train to Rovaniemi and bus to Kilpisjärvi. Saarijärvi-Kilpisjärvi was windy/rainy with boulder fields, wet marshes, fatigue and a long-feeling Norway passage. Supports demanding-weather framing rather than geometry decisions.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi reported as 18 km when including access/logistics from camping/supermarket; hut table gives Kilpis camping/hotel to Saarijärvi as 11.8 km. Trail fairly easy to follow, slight climb to Tsahkaljärvi, many day hikers early then quieter; strong wind at Saarijärvi and author slept inside hut.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Low wooden posts with orange tips can disappear behind rocks. Early terrain rocky and challenging despite moderate ascent. Dry conditions made water levels low; normal water levels likely mean wetter, muddier and more slippery travel. Intermittent mobile coverage at Saarijärvi.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Stage listed as 12 km. First kilometer from nature centre to Tsahkaljärvi was easy, then terrain became progressively rockier with wet patches. Good tent spot found about 0.5 km before huts; hut surroundings very rocky.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Full Kilpisjärvi-Halti reviews note poles are useful for rocky terrain and crossings, route condition was reported great in late summer 2023, huts/toilets clean and used. Not stage-specific.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi reported as 13 km and 3:25. Start on gravel walking route, path clear/easy to follow, then winding through rocks and small mounds. Saarijärvi hut visible long before arrival; tent spots limited due rocky/uneven ground, with better spots across a bridge.

records.title: condition Reports
records.summary: Older but detailed report: route from Tsahkaljärvi ascends moderately by a reindeer fence and briefly enters Norway. Saarijärvi not ideal for tenting because of rocks; water taken from streams/rivers as personal practice.

records.title: source Contradictions
records.summary: Reisa overview says 22 km; Reisa poster says 20 km; E1 GPX and OSM E1 parent geometry measure about 19.36 km; OSM child relation 9517537 tags 19.4 km but current members measure only about 17.09 km; field road exits are about 9-12 km.

records.title: source Contradictions
records.summary: OSM relation 9517537 is named Buletjávri-Čunovuohppi and omits the Kautokeino-to-Buletjávri approach. The OSM E1 parent relation or E1 GPX includes the missing approach.

records.title: source Contradictions
records.summary: Reisa still lists Madam Bongos fjellstue as endpoint, but Brønnøysund says the entity was deleted 2019-05-28, UT says the fjellstue is closed, municipal strategy calls Čunovuohppi the former fjellstue, and municipal minutes downgraded the road due no operation.

records.title: source Contradictions
records.summary: Reisa names Kautokeino but does not publish a precise terminus. E1/OSM route endpoint is about 180 m from Kartverket town centre and about 0.27 km from Kautokeino rådhus stop.

records.title: source Contradictions

records.title: rules To Normalize
records.summary: Summer-marked hiking route; not a normal winter route. | Freedom-to-roam norms allow responsible camping in many places, but protected areas override this. | Movement is restricted to marked routes in snow-free season; camping/route rules must be checked before import. | Norway's woodland fire ban period runs 15 April to 15 September; Reisa/protected-area rules and local fire bans must be checked. | County/municipal fire bans override normal permissions and must be checked before publication. | A summer thru-hike with a dog is likely not viable because dog rules vary and some national parks/protected areas prohibit dogs outside winter/spring exceptions. | The route crosses active Sami homeland and reindeer-herding areas. Avoid disturbing reindeer, close gates, avoid tenting near reindeer fences/enclosures, and respect herding work. | Water is generally abundant but fords are a major safety factor. Several sections involve unbridged streams/rivers; high water after snowmelt or heavy rain can force detours or make crossings unsafe. | Do not rely on mobile coverage. Finnish and Laponia sources warn of coverage gaps; cabin books and emergency planning matter. Offline maps, map/compass and satellite/PLB are recommended for remote sections.
